issues.issue: The representation carves out "litigation with respect to which pleadings or documents have been filed with a court, but not served on the Master Servicer" and is limited to matters with a "reasonable likelihood" of a material adverse effect. The combination of the carve-out and the undefined likelihood threshold leaves the representation's reach open.

The sentence preserves representations after "any termination of the Master Servicer hereunder", but the Master Servicer's termination and succession are governed by Article VII of this Agreement and by the Indenture, and no termination mechanic appears in Article II. The interaction of this survival clause with those provisions is not spelled out.

Section 2.08 lets the Indenture Trustee enforce the Sponsor's repurchase obligations "without joinder of the Depositor or the Issuing Entity", while Section 2.03(a) contemplates that the Depositor will take enforcement action at the request of the Issuing Entity or Indenture Trustee. Who may enforce, and on whose initiative, requires the two to be read together.

The Master Servicer is required to "monitor", "reconcile" and "coordinate corrective adjustments" to the Servicer's HELOC data, yet the last sentence entitles it to "conclusively rely" on that same data with "no liability for any errors". The two duties in the same section cannot both be given full effect.

This paragraph gives record access to a closed list (Noteholders, Note Insurer, the FDIC and its agents) and permits a charge covering actual copying costs, whereas Section 4.07(a) grants access to a broader group including the Office of Thrift Supervision and other regulators and states it is "to be afforded without charge". The two access regimes differ in both beneficiaries and cost.

The enumerated foreclosure documents are followed by a catch-all — "(iv) enforce any other rights or remedies provided by the Mortgage Note or Security Instrument or otherwise available at law or equity" — whose breadth against the specific items (i)-(iii) is undefined. What documents the Indenture Trustee must execute is left open.

Whether to terminate or notice the Servicer rests on the Master Servicer's own "judgment" and on it taking "such other action as it deems appropriate", with no standard supplied. The extent of that discretion is a matter of construction.

Subsection (a) makes termination of the Servicer a matter of the Master Servicer's judgment, while Section 4.02(b) states that the Master Servicer "shall ... terminate the rights and obligations of the Servicer" if the Servicer fails to perform, "subject to the preceding paragraph". Whether the duty is mandatory or discretionary cannot be settled from either subsection alone.

Enforcement is to be carried out "to such an extent and at such time as the Master Servicer, in its good faith business judgment, would require were it the owner of the HELOCs", a hypothetical-owner standard with no measurable benchmark. Whether particular inaction breaches it turns on that phrase.

The mandatory "shall ... terminate the rights and obligations of the Servicer" is expressly made "subject to the preceding paragraph", i.e. Section 4.02(a), which leaves termination to the Master Servicer's judgment and to what it "deems appropriate". The obligation and its qualifier point in opposite directions.

Reimbursement is to come from the Master Servicer Collection Account "as Extraordinary Trust Fund Expenses", but the permitted withdrawals from that account are set by Section 5.03, which is not cross-referenced here. Whether such withdrawals are permitted requires reading the two together.

The one-sentence disclaimer — "it will not assume liability for the representations and warranties of the Servicer it replaces" — does not say whether it covers only pre-succession reps or also continuing servicing obligations, and "acts as a servicer" is undefined. Its scope as a liability shield is contestable on its face.

The alternative to insurance is self-insurance "if LaSalle Bank National Association maintains with any Rating Agency the equivalent of a long term unsecured debt rating of 'A'", and any policy need only be "in such form and amount generally acceptable for entities serving as master servicers or trustees". Neither the rating equivalence nor "generally acceptable" supplies an applicable boundary.

Section 4.04 states that "[t]he Master Servicer shall master service the HELOCs" with power to consent to transfers and to effectuate foreclosure, whereas Section 4.01 confines the Master Servicer to supervising, monitoring and overseeing the Servicer, who services the HELOCs under the Servicing Agreement. The allocation of servicing functions between the two sections is not consistent.

"[T]he original Mortgagor may be released from liability in accordance with the Servicing Agreement" does not say who exercises the release or on what conditions, and "enforceable due-on-sale clauses" is left to be judged case by case. The permissive "may" gives the sentence no determinate operation.

The return obligation runs until "the need therefor ... as it reasonably determines, no longer exists unless the related HELOC shall be liquidated, in which case ... the Mortgage File shall be released" — an exception that directs release of a file already released. As drafted the sentence loops and does not say what happens on liquidation.

"The Master Servicer shall, and (to the extent provided in the Servicing Agreement or this Agreement) enforce the obligation of the Servicer to, provide access" is missing the verb governing "shall", leaving unclear whether the Master Servicer must itself provide access or only enforce the Servicer's duty. The grammatical break changes the obligation.

Access here is "to be afforded without charge", while the corresponding access paragraph in Section 4.01 permits a charge covering the Master Servicer's, Securities Administrator's and Indenture Trustee's actual costs of photocopying. The two cannot both govern the same request without reconciliation.

The sentence runs "shall be held by the Master Servicer for and on behalf of the Issuing Entity, the Indenture Trustee, the Noteholders and the Certificateholders shall be and remain the sole and exclusive property of the Issuing Entity" with no conjunction between the two predicates. Whether the funds are held for four beneficiaries or owned solely by the Issuing Entity depends on repairing the break.

"[N]o earthquake or other additional insurance is to be required" pairs a specific exclusion with an open-ended "other additional insurance", leaving unclear what kinds of coverage the exclusion reaches. The saving reference to laws "as shall require such additional insurance" does not fix the boundary.

Insurance amounts are deposited into the Master Servicer Collection Account but are said to be "subject to withdrawal pursuant to Sections 5.05 and 5.06", which by the table of contents govern the Payment Account and the Net WAC Cap Rate Carryover Reserve Account; permitted withdrawals from the Master Servicer Collection Account are in Section 5.03. The cross-references do not match the account named.

The Master Servicer must enforce the Servicer's duty to take "such actions (including the negotiation, settlement, compromise or enforcement of the insured's claim) as shall be necessary to realize recovery", with no standard for necessity or for an acceptable compromise. The extent of the enforcement duty is left to be construed.
